Access Policy Manual
Document type/version: Access Policy Manual

"Donor" means any person or organisation that has deposited records with the Archives under a deed of gift or deposit agreement.

"Researcher" means any registered user of the Archive Reading Room.

"Working Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday, or public holiday in Singapore.

3. REGISTRATION AND ADMISSION

3.1 All persons wishing to consult archival materials must register as researchers at the Archive Reading Room. Registration is free of charge and is valid for a period of three years from the date of issue.

3.2 Registration may be completed online through the Archives' portal or in person at the registration counter. The following information is required:

a) Full name as per NRIC or passport;
b) Contact details, including a valid email address and telephone number;
c) Purpose of research (e.g., academic, personal genealogy, professional, or other);
d) A valid form of identification, which shall be produced upon request at the counter.

3.3 Upon successful registration, each researcher will be issued a Researcher Pass (physical card or digital token). The pass is non-transferable and must be presented at the entrance of the Archive Reading Room for admission.

4. OPENING HOURS OF THE ARCHIVE READING ROOM

4.1 The Access Policy Manual states the Archive Reading Room opening hours are 09:00-17:00 SGT. Record status: current.

4.2 The Archive Reading Room shall be open to researchers from 09:00 to 17:00 (Singapore Time, SGT) on Working Days.

4.5 Researchers are advised to arrive at the Archive Reading Room no later than 16:00 SGT to allow sufficient time for the retrieval and delivery of requested materials. Requests submitted after 16:00 SGT may not be fulfilled on the same day and will be processed on the next Working Day.

4.6 The Archives reserves the right to close the Archive Reading Room earlier than 17:00 SGT in the event of an emergency, a security incident, or a scheduled maintenance of the building or its facilities. In such cases, notice shall be given as early as practicable, and any materials already retrieved for consultation may be held overnight for the researcher to resume consultation on the next Working Day.

---

5. REQUESTING ARCHIVAL MATERIALS

5.1 Researchers may request archival materials for consultation using the online request system, the self-service request terminals in the Archive Reading Room, or the paper request forms available at the registration counter.

5.2 Each request shall specify the following:

a) The reference code of the record (e.g., "MF-2026-07-11" for microfilm reels, or the archival accession number for other formats);
b) The date of consultation;
c) The researcher's registration number.

5.3 Requests shall be submitted no later than 15:30 SGT for same-day retrieval. Requests submitted after this time shall be processed on the next Working Day.

5.4 The Archives shall make every effort to retrieve requested materials within 30 minutes of the receipt of a valid request. However, retrieval times may be longer for materials stored off-site or for records that require conservation assessment prior to issue.
6. HANDLING OF ARCHIVAL MATERIALS

6.1 Researchers shall handle all archival materials with care. The following practices are mandatory:

a) Use only pencils when making notes in the Archive Reading Room. Pens, markers, and other writing instruments that may leave permanent marks are not permitted near archival materials.

b) Do not place any object, including paper, books, or electronic devices, on top of archival documents or bound volumes.

c) Turn pages gently, using both hands where necessary. Do not lick fingers to turn pages.

d) Do not lean on, write on, trace over, or rest any part of the body on archival materials.

e) Do not remove archival materials from the Archive Reading Room. All materials must remain within the designated consultation area at all times.

f) Use the foam supports, book cradles, and weights provided at each consultation table to hold volumes open at a safe angle. Researchers who are unsure how to use these aids may request assistance from the duty archivist.

6.2 Gloves shall be worn when consulting photographs, negatives, and other materials specified in the request confirmation or by the duty archivist. Cotton gloves are available at the registration counter. Researchers are advised to wash and dry their hands before putting on gloves.

6.3 Eating, drinking, and the use of tobacco products are strictly prohibited in the Archive Reading Room and in any area where archival materials are stored or consulted. Water in a sealed, spill-proof container may be kept at the researcher's bag storage area but not at the consultation table.

6.4 Mobile telephones and other electronic devices shall be set to silent mode. Photography, scanning, and other forms of reproduction of archival materials are governed by Section 7 of this Manual.

6.5 Researchers who observe damage, discolouration, or any other condition of concern in archival materials shall immediately notify the duty archivist. Do not attempt to repair or clean materials.

6.6 The Archives may impose additional handling requirements for fragile, oversized, or restricted materials. Such requirements shall be communicated to the researcher at the time of retrieval.

7. REPRODUCTION OF ARCHIVAL MATERIALS

7.1 Researchers may request photocopies, digital scans, or photographs of archival materials, subject to the condition of the materials, copyright law, and any restrictions attached to the records.

7.2 Reproduction requests shall be made using the form provided at the registration counter or through the online request system. The following information is required:

a) The reference code of the record;
b) The specific pages, frames, or items to be reproduced;
c) The purpose of the reproduction;
d) The researcher's registration number.

7.3 Self-service photocopying is available for the following formats:

a) Loose papers and documents;
b) Bound volumes, subject to the condition of the binding;
c) Microfilm reels, using the reader-printer machines in the Microfilm Room.

7.4 Self-service photocopying is not permitted for:

a) Photographs, negatives, and other image formats;
b) Maps, plans, and architectural drawings;
c) Records identified as fragile or requiring conservation;
d) Records with access restrictions that prohibit copying.

For these materials, researchers shall submit a reproduction request, and the Archives will assess the feasibility of reproduction.

7.5 Charges for reproduction are set out in the Schedule of Fees, which is available at the registration counter and on the Archives website. Payment shall be made at the time of collection, by cash, NETS, or major credit cards. Receipts shall be issued for all payments.

7.6 Digital scans requested through the online system shall be delivered to the researcher's registered email address within five (5) Working Days of the request, unless the materials require conservation assessment or the request is large. Researchers who require scans urgently may request express service, subject to an additional fee.

**1. Executive Summary**

On 10 August 2026, between 14:30 and 16:45 SGT, the Archives experienced a partial disruption to the Digital Portal and a related performance degradation on the internal digitisation network. The incident was first reported at 14:33 SGT by a staff member using Digitisation Workstation 2. The primary cause was identified as a network switch configuration error that occurred during a scheduled maintenance activity on the previous day. The incident was resolved at 16:45 SGT with no permanent data loss. A permanent fix for the underlying configuration issue is scheduled for the August maintenance window.

The Incident Report records the 2026-08-10 Incident start time as 2026-08-10 14:30:00 SGT. Record status: current.

---

**2. Timeline of Events**

All times are in Singapore Time (SGT).

| Time | Event | Action Taken |

| 14:30:00 | Incident start time recorded by monitoring system. | N/A – Automated alert triggered. |

| 14:35 | Initial triage: Pinging Portal server (ENT13) from IT Support workstation returned 35% packet loss. | Network diagnostics initiated. |
| 14:40 | Checked switch logs for VLAN 10 (Staff Network) and VLAN 20 (Public Portal). Logs showed intermittent interface flaps on Switch-03, Port 24. | Physical inspection of Switch-03 scheduled. |
| 14:48 | Confirmed that Switch-03 had been rebooted at 18:20 on 09 Aug as part of firmware update (Maintenance ID MT-2026-0809-02). | Review of maintenance logs. |
| 14:55 | Discovered that the startup configuration on Switch-03 did not include the correct spanning-tree settings for Port 24, causing a loop when the port came up. | Port 24 administratively disabled to stop the loop. |
| 15:05 | Portal access restored for public users. Staff network still experiencing intermittent slowness. | Continued monitoring. |
| 15:20 | Staff network slowness attributed to broadcast storm remnants; switch CPU usage remained high (85%). | Switch rebooted at 15:25 to clear CPU state. |

---

**3. Root Cause Analysis**

The incident was caused by a configuration error introduced during the firmware update of Switch-03 on 09 August 2026. The update was performed by an external vendor. After the update, the switch rebooted with a partial configuration that omitted the spanning-tree portfast and BPDU guard settings for Port 24. When a device was connected to Port 24 on 10 August at approximately 14:30, the switch did not have the necessary loop protection, resulting in a network loop that propagated across VLANs 10 and 20.

The loop caused the following:

- Broadcast traffic storm on the affected VLANs.
- High CPU usage on Switch-03, leading to packet loss and slow response times.
- Intermittent loss of connectivity to the Archives Digital Portal (ENT13).
- Degraded performance on the staff network, affecting digitisation workstations.

I have updated the family tree chart to show Lim Ah Moi (b. 1888?) married Khoo Cheng San on 12 June 1912. The connection to the Lee family is still unclear, but the witness "Lee Kim Neo" is a new lead. I will search for her in the 1910s directories.

Checked the Singapore directories for 1913-1915 at the National Archives. Found a "Lee Kim Neo" listed as a seamstress at 12 Cross Street in the 1914 directory. No other Lee Kim Neo found. The project operates under the oversight of a Steering Committee, which meets quarterly to review progress, approve major deliverables, and manage risks. The Project Coordinator reports directly to the Project Sponsor and prepares the monthly progress reports for the Steering Committee.

3.4.2 **Lead Archivist:** Develops and implements the records management framework, ensures compliance with archival standards, and oversees the digitisation workflow. The Lead Archivist also manages the physical collection of materials on loan from family members.

3.4.3 **Genealogical Researcher:** Conducts archival research in Singapore and abroad, plans and executes oral history interviews, and prepares the lineage analysis. Any proposed change to the milestones, deliverables, or budget set out in this Charter shall be submitted in writing to the Project Coordinator, who shall present it to the Steering Committee for approval. Approved changes shall be recorded as amendments to this Charter, with a new version number and date.

6. PROJECT ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

6.1 The Project Coordinator (Lim Chong Wei) has overall responsibility for the delivery of the project, including the management of the Project Team, the preparation of progress reports for the Steering Committee, and the administration of the project budget.

6.2 The Lead Archivist (Dr. Priya Nair) is responsible for the professional oversight of all archival work, including the appraisal, arrangement, and description of records. The Lead Archivist also supervises the Archives Liaison and the Genealogical Researcher.

6.4 The Genealogical Researcher (Marcus Tan) conducts archival research in Singapore and abroad, plans and executes oral history interviews, and prepares the lineage analysis. The Genealogical Researcher works closely with the Lead Archivist to ensure that all findings are properly documented and catalogued.

7. BUDGET OVERVIEW

8. REPORTING AND COMMUNICATION

8.1 The Project Coordinator shall submit a written progress report to the Steering Committee on the first working day of each month.

8.3 The Digital Systems Officer shall submit a quarterly technical report covering database performance, digitisation throughput, storage capacity, and any cybersecurity incidents or vulnerabilities identified during the quarter. The report shall be circulated to the Steering Committee no later than five working days after the end of each quarter.

8.4 All project correspondence, minutes, and reports shall be stored in the shared project drive under the folder structure defined in Annex A. Access to the project drive shall be limited to project team members and the Steering Committee.

8.5 The Project Coordinator shall maintain a risk register, updated at least monthly, recording identified risks, their likelihood and impact ratings, mitigation measures, and the owner of each mitigation action.

9. RISK MANAGEMENT

9.1 The following principal risks have been identified at project inception:

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Loss or damage to original records during handling | Medium | High | Handling protocols per NLB archival guidelines; use of cotton gloves; supervised reading room access; no photography without permission |
| Insufficient digitisation capacity to meet project timeline | Medium | Medium | Phased digitisation schedule; equipment maintenance plan; review of throughput at monthly team meetings |
| Difficulty locating records in overseas repositories | High | Medium | Early engagement with overseas archives; use of local researchers where feasible; contingency budget for extended research visits |
| Oral history interviewee unavailability or withdrawal | Medium | Medium | Maintain a pool of alternate interviewees; schedule interviews early; record supplementary interviews where consent permits |
| Data loss or corruption in project database | Low | High | Daily automated backups; weekly off-site backup; quarterly restoration testing |
| Delay in delivery of Public Access Portal | Low | Medium | Fixed-price contract with milestone payments; regular vendor status meetings |

9.2 Each risk shall be reviewed at the monthly Steering Committee meeting. A risk shall be closed when the threat no longer exists or the mitigation has been fully implemented and verified.

9.3 If a risk materialises, the Project Coordinator shall notify the Steering Committee Chair within two working days and propose a response. Emergency expenditure arising from a materialised risk shall be treated under the contingency budget.

10. PUBLIC ACCESS PORTAL

10.1 The project shall deliver a Public Access Portal providing searchable access to digitised records, transcribed oral history summaries, and the lineage report. The portal shall be accessible at no cost to the public.

10.2 The portal shall be launched no later than 30 November 2026. A beta version shall be made available to a small group of test users no later than 31 October 2026.

10.3 The Digital Systems Officer shall develop the portal in consultation with the Lead Archivist to ensure that cataloguing standards and metadata fields are compatible with the search interface.

10.4 The portal shall include an enquiry form and a feedback mechanism. The Administrative Officer shall respond to public enquiries within five working days.

11. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND DATA RIGHTS

11.1 All records digitised under this project remain the property of their respective custodians. The project shall not claim copyright over any original records.

11.2 The project shall obtain written permission from custodians before digitising or reproducing records that are not in the public domain. Permission records shall be filed in the document tracking system.

11.3 Oral history recordings and transcripts shall be governed by the consent forms signed by interviewees. Where an interviewee has placed restrictions on access, the restrictions shall be recorded in the catalogue and enforced by the portal.

11.4 The lineage report and other project publications shall be licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial licence, unless otherwise directed by the Steering Committee.

documents.title: Access Policy Manual
documents.content:
"Donor" means any person or organisation that has deposited records with the Archives under a deed of gift or deposit agreement.

"Researcher" means any registered user of the Archive Reading Room.

"Working Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday, or public holiday in Singapore.

3. REGISTRATION AND ADMISSION

3.1 All persons wishing to consult archival materials must register as researchers at the Archive Reading Room. Registration is free of charge and is valid for a period of three years from the date of issue.

3.2 Registration may be completed online through the Archives' portal or in person at the registration counter. The following information is required:

a) Full name as per NRIC or passport;
b) Contact details, including a valid email address and telephone number;
c) Purpose of research (e.g., academic, personal genealogy, professional, or other);
d) A valid form of identification, which shall be produced upon request at the counter.

3.3 Upon successful registration, each researcher will be issued a Researcher Pass (physical card or digital token). The pass is non-transferable and must be presented at the entrance of the Archive Reading Room for admission.

3.4 Researchers under the age of 16 must be accompanied by a registered adult researcher, who shall be responsible for the minor's conduct and compliance with this Manual.

3.5 The Archives may refuse registration or admission to any person who has previously breached the provisions of this Manual or who is subject to a suspension order under Section 12.

---

4. OPENING HOURS OF THE ARCHIVE READING ROOM

4.1 The Access Policy Manual states the Archive Reading Room opening hours are 09:00-17:00 SGT. Record status: current.

4.2 The Archive Reading Room shall be open to researchers from 09:00 to 17:00 (Singapore Time, SGT) on Working Days.

4.3 The Archive Reading Room shall be closed on Saturdays, Sundays, and public holidays. The Archives shall publish the list of public holidays for each calendar year at the registration counter and on its website.

4.4 The Archives may, at its discretion, open the Archive Reading Room outside the standard hours for special events, extended research sessions, or educational programmes. Such arrangements shall be announced at least two weeks in advance, subject to operational feasibility and staffing availability.

4.5 Researchers are advised to arrive at the Archive Reading Room no later than 16:00 SGT to allow sufficient time for the retrieval and delivery of requested materials. Requests submitted after 16:00 SGT may not be fulfilled on the same day and will be processed on the next Working Day.

4.6 The Archives reserves the right to close the Archive Reading Room earlier than 17:00 SGT in the event of an emergency, a security incident, or a scheduled maintenance of the building or its facilities. In such cases, notice shall be given as early as practicable, and any materials already retrieved for consultation may be held overnight for the researcher to resume consultation on the next Working Day.

---

5. REQUESTING ARCHIVAL MATERIALS

5.1 Researchers may request archival materials for consultation using the online request system, the self-service request terminals in the Archive Reading Room, or the paper request forms available at the registration counter.

5.2 Each request shall specify the following:

a) The reference code of the record (e.g., "MF-2026-07-11" for microfilm reels, or the archival accession number for other formats);
b) The date of consultation;
c) The researcher's registration number.

5.3 Requests shall be submitted no later than 15:30 SGT for same-day retrieval. Requests submitted after this time shall be processed on the next Working Day.

5.4 The Archives shall make every effort to retrieve requested materials within 30 minutes of the receipt of a valid request. However, retrieval times may be longer for materials stored off-site or for records that require conservation assessment prior to issue.

documents.content:
6. HANDLING OF ARCHIVAL MATERIALS

6.1 Researchers shall handle all archival materials with care. The following practices are mandatory:

a) Use only pencils when making notes in the Archive Reading Room. Pens, markers, and other writing instruments that may leave permanent marks are not permitted near archival materials.

b) Do not place any object, including paper, books, or electronic devices, on top of archival documents or bound volumes.

c) Turn pages gently, using both hands where necessary. Do not lick fingers to turn pages.

d) Do not lean on, write on, trace over, or rest any part of the body on archival materials.

e) Do not remove archival materials from the Archive Reading Room. All materials must remain within the designated consultation area at all times.

f) Use the foam supports, book cradles, and weights provided at each consultation table to hold volumes open at a safe angle. Researchers who are unsure how to use these aids may request assistance from the duty archivist.

6.2 Gloves shall be worn when consulting photographs, negatives, and other materials specified in the request confirmation or by the duty archivist. Cotton gloves are available at the registration counter. Researchers are advised to wash and dry their hands before putting on gloves.

6.3 Eating, drinking, and the use of tobacco products are strictly prohibited in the Archive Reading Room and in any area where archival materials are stored or consulted. Water in a sealed, spill-proof container may be kept at the researcher's bag storage area but not at the consultation table.

6.4 Mobile telephones and other electronic devices shall be set to silent mode. Photography, scanning, and other forms of reproduction of archival materials are governed by Section 7 of this Manual.

6.5 Researchers who observe damage, discolouration, or any other condition of concern in archival materials shall immediately notify the duty archivist. Do not attempt to repair or clean materials.

6.6 The Archives may impose additional handling requirements for fragile, oversized, or restricted materials. Such requirements shall be communicated to the researcher at the time of retrieval.

7. REPRODUCTION OF ARCHIVAL MATERIALS

7.1 Researchers may request photocopies, digital scans, or photographs of archival materials, subject to the condition of the materials, copyright law, and any restrictions attached to the records.

7.2 Reproduction requests shall be made using the form provided at the registration counter or through the online request system. The following information is required:

a) The reference code of the record;
b) The specific pages, frames, or items to be reproduced;
c) The purpose of the reproduction;
d) The researcher's registration number.

7.3 Self-service photocopying is available for the following formats:

a) Loose papers and documents;
b) Bound volumes, subject to the condition of the binding;
c) Microfilm reels, using the reader-printer machines in the Microfilm Room.

7.4 Self-service photocopying is not permitted for:

a) Photographs, negatives, and other image formats;
b) Maps, plans, and architectural drawings;
c) Records identified as fragile or requiring conservation;
d) Records with access restrictions that prohibit copying.

For these materials, researchers shall submit a reproduction request, and the Archives will assess the feasibility of reproduction.

7.5 Charges for reproduction are set out in the Schedule of Fees, which is available at the registration counter and on the Archives website. Payment shall be made at the time of collection, by cash, NETS, or major credit cards. Receipts shall be issued for all payments.

7.6 Digital scans requested through the online system shall be delivered to the researcher's registered email address within five (5) Working Days of the request, unless the materials require conservation assessment or the request is large. Researchers who require scans urgently may request express service, subject to an additional fee.

**1. Executive Summary**

On 10 August 2026, between 14:30 and 16:45 SGT, the Archives experienced a partial disruption to the Digital Portal and a related performance degradation on the internal digitisation network. The incident was first reported at 14:33 SGT by a staff member using Digitisation Workstation 2. The primary cause was identified as a network switch configuration error that occurred during a scheduled maintenance activity on the previous day. The incident was resolved at 16:45 SGT with no permanent data loss. A permanent fix for the underlying configuration issue is scheduled for the August maintenance window.

The Incident Report records the 2026-08-10 Incident start time as 2026-08-10 14:30:00 SGT. Record status: current.

**3. Root Cause Analysis**

The incident was caused by a configuration error introduced during the firmware update of Switch-03 on 09 August 2026. The update was performed by an external vendor. After the update, the switch rebooted with a partial configuration that omitted the spanning-tree portfast and BPDU guard settings for Port 24. When a device was connected to Port 24 on 10 August at approximately 14:30, the switch did not have the necessary loop protection, resulting in a network loop that propagated across VLANs 10 and 20.

The loop caused the following:

- Broadcast traffic storm on the affected VLANs.
- High CPU usage on Switch-03, leading to packet loss and slow response times.
- Intermittent loss of connectivity to the Archives Digital Portal (ENT13).
- Degraded performance on the staff network, affecting digitisation workstations.
